websiteToolWorkoutLogTemplate.title: Free printable workout log
websiteToolWorkoutLogTemplate.intro: Download a workout log to print, or a spreadsheet to fill in on a computer. Both are free, with no sign-up. The spreadsheet saves as a CSV that the Musclog app can import.

sections.title: What is in the printable log
body: Each sheet is one workout. At the top you write the date, the workout, your bodyweight and whether you lift in kg or lb. Below are twelve exercise rows with five sets each, a box for the weight and a box for the reps, and a Notes column for how hard a set felt or anything that hurt.
The PDF holds four sheets, so one print covers about a week or two. Print as many copies as you need. The sheets carry no program: you decide what goes in the rows.

sections.title: How to fill the spreadsheet
body: Write one row per set: the date, the workout name, the exercise, the set number, the weight and the reps. RPE and Notes are optional. Weight is a plain number in the unit you always use. Leave Reps empty for a timed set. RPE 10 is a set with nothing left, 9 leaves one rep and 8 leaves two.

The columns follow the layout Musclog's importer reads, so you do not have to convert anything. Save the Log sheet as a CSV file, then in the app open Settings, then Backups and data, then Import workouts. Musclog matches the exercise names to its catalogue and shows a review before it saves a single session.

sections.title: Paper, a spreadsheet or an app
body: Paper needs no battery and no account, and writing a set takes a few seconds. What it cannot do is look back for you: you read last week's sheet yourself to decide what to lift today.

A spreadsheet can add up your volume and chart a lift, if you build the formulas. Musclog does that and works out the next weight from your last session, with the reason shown, but the log is yours either way. It is a free, open-source app, your data stays on your device, and you can bring the spreadsheet above into it.
